PARTICIPANTS: DAVID M. FELTS DEXTER JONES BENJAMIN MORRIS H. JOSEPH EASTER TODD ROBINSON District 1 District 2 District 3 District 4 District 5 ALSO ATTENDING: ERIC S. POLLITT, County Administrator ASHLEY PILLAR, Finance Director /Deputy County Administrator MARY BETH SMITH, Human Resources Director Chairman Felts called the October 14, 2026, Work Session to order at 6:00 P.M. and determined a quorum was present. County Administrator Eric Pollitt offered the invocation, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance. Action: Chairman Felts moved to approve the agenda as presented. Motion carried unanimously. 1.A. Financial Policies (Part 1) County Administrator Eric Pollitt presented proposed financial standard operating procedures covering accounting, accounts payable, check signing, and procurement. Board Discussion & Requested Revisions: • Approval Thresholds: Clarified that invoice signature thresholds vary based on department size, and department heads had previously reviewed the draft policies with administration. • ACH Payments: Confirmed that all ACH/online payments require prior approval by the County Administrator before processing. • Small Purchase Procurement: Directed staff to establish clear minimum spending thresholds below which formal quotes are not required for routine purchases. • Implementation: Upon adoption, department heads will review the policies with staff for signed acknowledgment, and HR will incorporate them into new-hire onboarding. Next Steps: By consensus, the Board agreed to place the revised financial policies on the October Regular Meeting agenda for consideration. 1.B. Personnel Policies (Part 1) County Administrator Eric Pollitt and HR Director Maribeth Smith presented proposed personnel policy updates slated to take effect July 1, 2027. Board Discussion & Requested Revisions: • Constitutional Officers: Revise references from "County Administrator" to "County Administrator or applicable Constitutional Officer" throughout the document. • Terminology & Telework: Standardize terminology (using either "remote work" or "telework" consistently) and clarify that remote work arrangements require approval from both the department head and County Administrator. • Probationary Leave: New hires may use accrued annual leave during their six-month probationary period, provided the policy stipulates that unused accrued leave is forfeited if the employee separates prior to completing probation. • Parental/Elderly Care & Leave Sharing: Confirmed parental/elderly care leave follows the 12-month FMLA schedule without carryover, and leave sharing will be managed case-by-case without a formal leave bank. Next Steps: Staff will work with legal counsel over the next 30 days to incorporate these revisions and bring the updated policies back for the November or December Regular Meeting. 1.C. Fire & Emergency Services Ordinance Interim Fire Chief Tommy Hicks provided a departmental progress update and introduced proposed revisions to Chapter 62 (Fire and EMS) along with a new Emergency Management chapter. The County Attorney has completed legal review of the draft. Next Steps: By consensus, the Board agreed to place the ordinance on the October Regular Meeting agenda for further review and potential action. MOTION TO ADJOURN/CONTINUE MEETING There being no other business, Chairman Felts made a motion adjourn the October 14, 2026, work session at 7:13 P.M. Motion was approved unanimously. Felts, Jr., Chairman Amelia County Administrator Amelia County Board of Supervisors VIRGINIA: AT A REGULAR MEETING OF THE COUNTY OF AMELIA BOARD OF SUPERVISORS HELD AT THE AMELIA COUNTY ADMINISTRATION CONFERENCE ROOM ON WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 28, 2026. PARTICIPANTS: DAVID M. FELTS DEXTER JONES BENJAMIN MORRIS H. JOSEPH EASTER, IV TODD ROBINSON District 1 District 2 District 3 District 4 District 5 Board of Supervisors ALSO ATTENDING: ERIC S. POLLITT, COUNTY ADMINISTRATOR JEFF GORE, COUNTY ATTORNEY Chairman Felts called the October 28, 2026, Regular Meeting of the Amelia County Board of Supervisors to order at 7:00 P.M. and determined there was a quorum with all five members participating. Supervisor Morris offered the invocation, and everyone participated in the Pledge of Allegiance. APPROVE/AMEND THE AGENDA • Chairman Felts made a request to add a data center discussion to the agenda under New Business. • Supervisor Morris made a motion to accept the agenda as amended with one addition of adding the data center discussion. Motion was approved unanimously. CONSENT AGENDA o Supervisor Morris made a motion to approve the consent agenda as presented. Motion was approved unanimously. A. Approval of Minutes • September 23, 2026 Regular Meeting Minutes B. Amelia County Sheriff’s Office- VACORP Funds Claim #5437 C. Amelia County Sheriff’s Office- VACORP Funds Claim #6097 D. Amelia County Sheriff’s Office- VACORP Funds Claim #6097 E. Voting Authorization for Upcoming VACO Meeting RECOGNITIONS A. Amberly Eells – 2026 Public Service Award • Brian Wooton, Manager of Animal Control read his nomination for Amberly Eells to the Board. Ms. Eells was then presented with a recognition letter from the Board acknowledging her as a recipient of the Dr. Charles A. Robinson Award for Public Service in Animal Control. PUBLIC COMMENTS • Mike Whitaker (12110 Genito Road) with Amelia County AmRev250 Committee provided the Board with information regarding an update of the VA250 mobile museum experience on November 19th and 20th, 2026 as well as various monthly updates from the committee. 1 • Allison Crews (20600 Perkins Road) discussed the reporting of the monthly waste management host fees, the 5-year review of the waste management contract, and the Landfill Advisory Committee’s recent meeting. o County Administrator, Eric Pollitt addressed the concern of the monthly waste management host fees. He advised the Chairman and Board that those fees are in the monthly packets each month but have been moved to a different section and that Mr. Pollitt reads them aloud each meeting. STAFF/COMMITTEE/ORGANIZATIONAL REPORTS AND PRESENTATIONS A. VDOT Report: o Adam Brooks with VDOT discussed items they are working on throughout the county; removal of dead animals on the roads, replacement of pipe on Route 681, and primary and secondary mowing. o Chairman Felts advised Mr. Brooks of their goal to have the speed limit dropped at Route 360 and Goodes Bridge Road due to several accidents in that area. o Supervisors Jones reported a large pothole near 13507 Dykeland Road. o Supervisor Robinson asked about getting the road fixed at Wayside Avenue on Business Route 360. Supervisor Robinson reported that he received a call about speeding on Jennings Lane and inquired about putting a speed limit sign up at that location due to children and animals in that area. B. School Board Report: o Superintendent, Dr. Lori Harper, reported on the participation in the recent facilities tour, all of Amelia County Schools becoming fully accredited, and a budget development survey that is coming up soon. K12 enrollment is at 1,442 and PreK12 enrollment is at 1,512. ADM for September is 1,429.85. o Financial Reports: o Superintendent, Dr. Lori Harper, presented financial reports as of September FY26 and the FY28 budget process. No questions were asked. C. J.L. Hamner Library Report: o Director, Keith McFarlane provided an update for the library programming and introduced their new employee, Riley Smith, Outreach Coordinator. D. Concert Summary Report: o Deputy Director of Parks & Recreation, Isaiah LeBlanc provided an overview of the Music on the Green concert, including a summary of the event and its overall outcome. E. Staff Reports: o Extension Office Quarterly Report: Mackenzie Gunn provided an update on programming. FINANCE A. Action Required Appropriations • ALA Grant-Library |Action o Supervisor Easter made a motion to approve the appropriation request of $10,000 as it requires no additional funding from the County. Motion was approved unanimously. • Salary Appropriation-Clerk’s Office |Action 2 • o Supervisor Easter made a motion to approve the appropriation request for $3,488.90 as it requires no additional funding from the County. Motion was approved unanimously. Supervisor Easter asked about the status of the Board receiving the monthly financial summary report vs. the summary they are being provided. Mr. Pollitt advised that he is composing a template and working with the Treasurer, Stephanie Coleman, to put some numbers together to provide the Board with CIP and quarterly updates. B. Informational Appropriations • None. COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT A. Community Development Monthly Report B. Environmental Department Report C. DMV Agent Compensation Statement and Payment Report COUNTY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT A. COAD Monthly Report • Mr. Pollitt provided an overview report of the ICMA Conference to the Board & thanked them for their support with allowing him to attend the event. • Mr. Pollitt reported that Riverstreet has officially declared bankruptcy. Mr. Pollitt also reminded the Board of a work session set up for November 12th to discuss the future of the broadband project for Amelia County. Mr. Pollitt is working with County Attorney Jeff Gore, on options to present to the Board. • Mr. Pollitt reported that he and Craig Meadows with Berkley Group, are working to finalize the report from the Board Retreat. The report is expected to be ready for presentation at the November meeting. B. YTD FY26 Waste Management Host Fees • Monthly fees are $239, 981.12 OLD BUSINESS A. Alternative Dates for November & December 2026 Board Meetings | Action • Supervisor Easter made a motion to approve the resolution with the minor date correction of November 24th not November 25th. Motion was approved unanimously. NEW BUSINESS A. Committee Appointments 1. Social Services Advisory Board Nomination (1) • Supervisor Jones made a motion to accept Lauren Whittington’s nomination to join the Social Services Advisory Board on an unexpired term. Motion was approved unanimously. B. Fire & Emergency Services Ordinance |Action • Supervisor Morris made a motion direct staff to advertise the proposed Fire & EMS and Emergency Management ordinances, as presented, for adoption at the regular November board meeting. Motion was approved unanimously. C. Financial Policies Part 1 |Action • Supervisor Easter made a motion to adopt the financial policies as presented. Motion was approved unanimously. 3 D. Cross Connection Control Program Ordinance Update |Action • Sam Carroll with B&B Consultants presented to the Board on cross connection control and backflow prevention. • Supervisor Easter made a motion to authorize staff and the County Attorney to advertise the proposed ordinance for consideration at the November Board of Supervisors meeting. Motion was approved unanimously. E. Return of Tangible Personal Property |Discussion • Supervisor Easter requested that staff move forward with an ordinance change to eliminate the requirement to return personal property tax forms, where permitted by state law. He also suggested offsetting the fees currently budgeted for these forms through an increase in the personal property tax rate during the next budget cycle. • Chairman Felts expressed that he was not in favor of eliminating the forms, noting that they provide the Commissioner of the Revenue with necessary information to properly assess vehicles. Supervisor Jones commented that some citizens delay returning the forms and are subject to penalties for doing so. Supervisor Robinson stated that additional research is needed to address outstanding questions, including the potential financial impact, before moving forward with the proposal. F. Data Centers |Discussion • Chairman Felts reported that he attended a data center training session presented by the CRC at Southside Virginia Community College. He stated that his main takeaway from the training was the importance of having policies and procedures in place to prepare for the potential arrival of data centers in the County. He requested that the Board provide direction to staff to work with the Planning Commission and Board of Zoning Appeals to develop a plan that will ensure the County is prepared for potential future development. All board members agreed. Mr. Pollitt confirmed that the Berkley Group would be directed to assist with developing more restrictive ordinance language regarding data centers to better address the County’s future needs and concerns. Felts o Attended Piedmont Regional Jail meeting; residents in September. o CRC-training on data center o Attended CMPT Meeting for Supervisor Robinson. o Attended the Music on the Green Concert; great. District 2-The Honorable Dexter Jones o Attended CRC meeting-BOOMS project. William Coleman provided a short summary of how the BOOMS meeting went. District 3-The Honorable Benjamin Morris o Attended the BOOMS meeting. o Ponce Store update; got paved and new signs are posted. District 4-The Honorable Joseph Easter o Reminder of Harvest Fest on November 7th; 3rd year. District 5-The Honorable Todd Robinson o No PSR Meeting this month. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Board of Supervisors of Amelia County request permission from the Virginia Department of Transportation to close the following streets on Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 4:00 P.M. to 6:00 P.M. • Wayside Ave (Route 605), Goodes Bridge Rd (Bus 360), Amelia St (Route 1005), Church St (Route 1003), Washinton St (Route 38), Court St (Route 1007), and Virginia St (Route 1009) AND FURTHER BE IT RESOLVED that the applicants for the Special Event Permit shall be responsible for providing the Virginia Department of Transportation the required map showing the streets to be closed, method of closing the streets, method of traffic control at each intersection and detour routes with approved markings.
